chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr and Ibn Abi Umeyr, both together, from Ma'mar ibn Yahya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the man who performs Zihaar from his wife: Is the emancipation of a newborn slave permissible in the expiation? He said: Every emancipation is permissible in which is the newborn, except in the expiation for killing, for indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'So free a believing slave,' meaning by that one who has accepted (Islam) who has reached the age of discretion.

key_terms.يُظَاهِرُ: Performs Zihaar (a pre-Islamic and early Islamic form of divorce where a husband likens his wife to his mother's back)

ai.seo_question: Can a newborn slave be freed as expiation for Zihaar or killing?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while freeing a newborn slave is generally valid for most expiations, it is excluded for the expiation of killing, which specifically requires a 'free believing slave' (raqabah mu'minah). The Imam interprets 'mu'minah' in this context as indicating a slave who has reached the age of discretion (balagh), distinguishing it from the general permissibility of younger slaves in other contexts like Zihaar. This ruling highlights the precise linguistic and legal nuances applied by the Imams in deriving fiqh from Quranic terminology.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr and Ibn Abu Umeyr, both together from Ma’mar Bin Yahya, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I asked himasws about the man who did ‘Zihaar’ from his wife. Is it allowed to free a new-born (slave) regarding the expiation?’ So heasws said: ‘Every emancipation is allowed in which is the new-born except regarding the expiation for the killing, for Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [4:92] he should free a believing slave, Meaning by that one who has accepted (Al Islam) who has reached the (age of) wrongdoing’.
en.sarwar: 15. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr and ibn abu ‘Umayr all from Mu’ammar ibn Yahya who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

about the case of a man who involves himself in al- Zihar against his wife; if it is permissible to free a newborn slave for Kaffarah (expiation). He (the Imam) said, ‘Every kind of Kaffarah (expiation) that requires freeing of a slave, freeing of a newborn slave is sufficient for it except for murder; Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, says, “. . . then set free a believing slave.” [4:92] He has meant thereby one who affirms the faith and is of the age of being held responsible for violating an oath.’”
